title: I Printed the Community-Kitchen Hood Timer After They Cooked Past the Beep

parts.text: I booked hood 1 until 8:00 p.m. and at 8:06 a catering crew was still reducing stock with the beep ignored. The wall said: HOOD FOLLOWS THE BEEP. CLEAN THE FILTER. NEXT COOK STARTS. I was thirty-seven, meal-train, holding a tray of uncooked pans. Crew lead Omar kept stirring. "Catering is the hood." I photographed the beep log, the wall, and their stock on my start. Then I logged an overtime. At 8:14 the kitchen coordinator asked why Omar's stock was on a post-beep still. I asked once, then I documented twice. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The kitchen coordinator can see catering stock on hood 1 after the 8:00 beep.

social.video_title: They reduced stock past the hood beep into my slot — Part 1/2
social.description: Community kitchen, uncooked pans, and an ignored beep. I logged overtime. Would you have photographed the stock?

parts.text: Omar called it a simmer until the coordinator asked for the log. I printed the overtime, the photo, and the wall. Stock left. Omar simmered on a booked leftover and told crews simmers were always about optics. Optics is a word catering uses when a beep exists. Hood policy now has a second line: CATERING ENDS. I keep the start. Omar books. The hood finally sounds like a timer, not a restaurant. The room sounds like a room again, not a title. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.

social.description: Overtime log, cleared hood, and a second line. Was a simmer ever post-beep?
